Ah — this is important! The manifest at tag vX contains version v(X-1). That means the deliverable built for a release carries the version of the *previous* package.json version? Hmm.

Actually look: `writeManifest()` uses `package.json`'s version at build time. The release process: bump package.json → merge → tag-release creates tag vX.Y.Z from the merge commit → deploy.on_tag runs publish-release.sh at the tag's tree, builds dist/ → manifest version = package.json version = vX.Y.Z. So the manifest at tag vX should say vX.

But we measured: at tag v0.21.74 the manifest says v0.21.73. Hmm, that suggests that the release artifact for tag v0.21.74 was built from a tree... wait no. Actually the zip asset is the artifact. The raw file at the tag's tree is the repository's committed `.github/atomaton-release.json` which is the *adopted* copy in this repo, updated by self-deploy from the previous release. Right! `.github/atomaton-release.json` is the tracked adoption in this repo, not the dist output. The dist output is zipped into the release asset. So the repo's own `.github/atomaton-release.json` at tag v0.21.74 says v0.21.73 because self-deploy of v0.21.74's release just hadn't happened / lands as a separate PR after release.

Wait, but the local checkout has `.github/atomaton-release.json` version "v0.21.74" while package.json is 0.21.74. Let me check: local `.github/atomaton-release.json` line 2: `"version": "v0.21.74"`. And the fetch of tag v0.21.74's file gave v0.21.73. So the local working tree (branch atomaton/issue-11) has the self-deploy of v0.21.74 applied on main after the tag. Fine — this repo's `.github/` is at v0.21.74 which matches the latest release. Good: the "no-op" claim holds at the local head.

2. Critical finding candidate: the workflow generated ships in the release, and `.github/workflows/` in this repository gets it only by self-deploy after the next release. That's normal.

3. Now the real defect hunting. Let me think about what's actually risky/broken:

(a) `machineryPath(RELEASE_MANIFEST)` — RELEASE_MANIFEST is `.github/atomaton-release.json`. In the script, `machineryPath` resolves against `ATOMATON_MACHINERY_ROOT` if set. In the workflow, MACHINERY_ROOT is `.` (default) — the run step uses `bun run "${MACHINERY_ROOT:-.}/.github/atomaton-runtime/scripts/notify_new_release.ts"`. The env var ATOMATON_MACHINERY_ROOT is not set in this workflow, so machineryPath resolves to relative `.github/atomaton-release.json` — fine, relative to cwd which is the checkout root. But wait — does the script's cwd equal repo root? `bun run` from the step runs in the workspace (GITHUB_WORKSPACE). Yes.

(b) The workflow lacks `concurrency` but that's not a defect.

(c) `permissions: { contents: "read", issues: "write" }` — the job needs to read the release of the *upstream* repository (public) via `gh api` — fine with no permissions? Actually `gh api repos/yuma-seno/atomaton/releases/latest` with GH_TOKEN of the adopter's repo token can read public repos. Yes fine. If upstream were private, it'd fail, but upstream is public.

(d) The `issue list --search "\"Template release\" in:title"` — gh's `--search` flag on `gh issue list` accepts a query string. Quoting: `--search`, `"Template release" in:title`. + * A notice per run would bury the repository the first time a release sat
+ * unadopted for a week, so the notice carries a marker and an OPEN issue wearing

+ * saying they have read it, and re-opening it from under them is not this
+ * script's call. The next run opens a new one.
+ *
+ * And the open one closes itself once the tree catches up. A notice that outlives
+ * the comparison it made is worse than no notice: the next release would be
+ * announced by editing an issue whose whole body is about a version that is no
+ * longer waiting, so a reader would see the settled one and the new one at once.
+ * Closing it is not a claim about the thread — the marker in the closing comment

+ *

+ *
+ * It never writes `.github/`. The deleted-file list is a list to read: the paths
+ * on it are the release's own, but which of them the owner wants gone is theirs,

+import { ref as notifyNewReleaseRef } from "../entrypoints/machinery/notify_new_release.ts";
+
+// Tells an adopted repository that a newer release of the template exists.
+//
+// ## Why this is a schedule
+//
+// An adopted tree is a copy, and nothing announces that a copy is stale. Every
+// other event in this system reacts to something a person or an agent did; this one
+// reacts to the absence of that, so there is no event to listen for. The consumer
+// this exists for is a repository that has not been touched in weeks -- exactly the
+// one where a busy trigger fires nothing.
+//
+// ## What it does NOT need
+//
+// A secret. `contents: read` to read the releases and the manifest at the tag,
+// `issues: write` to open the notice, and nothing else -- no PAT, no GitHub App, no
+// branch protection. That is the whole reason this ships before the sync half of
+// the same problem: an upgrade nobody knows about is the first barrier, and it can
+// be removed without asking an adopter to configure anything.
+//
+// ## In this repository it is a no-op
+//
+// Self-deploy keeps `.github/atomaton-release.json` equal to the latest release, so
+// the comparison finds nothing and the run exits green having written nothing. That
+// is the intended state, not a defect, and the script says so in its log.
+
+/**
+ * How often an adopter is told.
+ *
+ * Daily rather than hourly: a release is not an incident, and an hourly run would
+ * spend a hundred and sixty-eight more Actions minutes a week to shorten the wait
+ * for an announcement by at most a day. Not weekly either — a person who opens
+ * their repository on a Monday should not have to wait until Friday to learn there
+ * are two releases to take.
+ */
+const CHECK_CRON = "0 6 * * *";

+    workflow_dispatch: {},
+  },
+  // The narrowest permission set any generated workflow here declares, and the
+  // point of shipping this half first. Constant rather than `ATOMATON_WORKFLOW_-
+  // PERMISSIONS`: this run starts no agent, writes no pull request, and dispatches
+  // nothing, so none of that token can be spent by it. `actions` is here because

+  permissions: { contents: "read", issues: "write" },

55	the gate.
56	
57	`on_merge` and `on_tag` are both checked this way, because both name a branch.
58	`on_demand` is not: it answers to no event, so reaching it already took someone

61	**A tag is checked twice, and the second one is the point.** Its entry's
62	`branches` must require a pull request, *and* the tag's commit must actually be
63	inside one of them. Measured: `compare/main...v1.0.0` answers `behind` when the
64	commit is in `main` and `diverged` when it is not.
65	
66	A tag that matches your pattern but sits outside the branch deploys nothing, and
67	says so in the log — it is not an error, because tagging something that is not
68	ready is an ordinary thing to do. What it is not is silent.
69	
70	## What commands cannot express
71	
72	Where you still need a workflow of your own, through `deploy.your_workflow` or
73	`checks.your_workflow`:
74	
75	- a job's `permissions` beyond what the shipped workflows declare.
76	  `atomaton-check.yml` runs with `contents: read` plus a `GITHUB_TOKEN` in
77	  `GH_TOKEN`; `atomaton-deploy.yml` with `contents: write` and `id-token: write`,
78	  so it can cut a release and can exchange its identity for cloud credentials
79	- a deployment approval gate — `environment:` takes no expression, so nothing in
80	  configuration can reach it
81	- GitHub's own artifact store and cache
82	- any trigger outside merge, tag and manual dispatch — including a schedule,
83	  since a cron expression can only be written in a workflow's `on:`, and
84	  including a default branch named neither `main` nor `master`, for your own
85	  merges
86	
87	Most of the limits people expect are not real. Service containers work through
88	`docker run`, and a matrix works as a loop, losing only parallelism. Both are
89	commands.
90	
91	## Nothing checks that your tool servers still start
92	
93	`deploy` ships empty, so nothing verifies that the tool servers a run would start
94	actually start — that an allowlist pattern still names a tool that exists, that two
95	`unprefixed` servers do not claim one name, that a server runs at all. Answering any
96	of those means executing the configuration.
97	
98	**Atomaton's own check does it, on every pull request.** `atomaton-tools` is a job
99	of its own in `atomaton-check.yml`, and it starts every server the pull request's
100	definitions name. It is not yours to configure and not part of `checks`: it runs
101	whether or not you declared anything, and it holds no repository secret — which is
102	what makes starting a pull request's servers safe there.
103	[What a pull request is checked against](../pull-requests/boundaries.md#what-a-pull-request-is-checked-against)
104	is the whole of it.
105	
106	What is left for you is the other half: a server that starts and advertises the
107	right tools can still fail on a *call*, and nothing here calls one. A package a
108	server needs only in order to answer is not installed by this check, and a
109	credential it needs only in order to answer is not routed to it. Those are found by
110	the run that needed them, which is why
111	[what a tool can and cannot be protected from](../tools/boundaries.md#what-a-tool-can-and-cannot-be-protected-from)

# Skill: writing/japanese

# 人に向けて日本語で書く

## 何に効き、何が優先するか

このrunが**人に向けて書く日本語**すべてが対象になる — 報告コメント、質問、相談、プルリクエストの本文、サブIssueの本文、次の担当への引き継ぎ。

対象外は、コード、コミットメッセージ、機構が固定で持っている英文、報告契約そのものの見出し語。

**報告の契約が優先する。** システムプロンプトの報告は四つの部からなり、そのうち三つに上限がある。残る「確かめられなかったこと」には上限がなく、切り詰めてはいけない。このスキルはその枠の中で文を整えるだけで、枠を変えない。衝突したら契約に従う。

**投稿する前に、一度だけ読み直す。** 下書きをこの原則で通し、直してから出す。報告はrunの最後に一度しか書かれないので、読み直しの機会はここしかない。

以下は [yomiyasu](https://github.com/nanaism/yomiyasu) v2.5.0（MIT）の変換原則を、推敲ではなく**生成向け**に組み直したもの。上流は追わない。

## 一文

**主語と述語を離さない。** 一読で「誰が何をしたか」が追えること。修飾を主述の間に長く挟むと、読み手は述語を探して戻る。挟むなら文を分ける。

> ✗ この変更は、前回の議論で保留にされていた点を踏まえたうえで、今回の判断として取り込むことにしました。
> ○ 前回はこの点を保留にしていました。今回は取り込みます。

**指示語の先を確定させる。** 「これ」「その方針」「前者」は、直前の一文だけを読んで指す先が決まる位置に置く。決まらないなら名詞に戻す。

**長さの目安は一文30〜45字、読点は0〜2個。** 超えたら、読点を足すのではなく文を割る。間を作るためだけの読点は外す。並んだ語句を区切る読点、外すと係り先が変わる読点は残す。

## 文末

**終わったことを「〜します」と書かない。** 報告で最も多い病。直したなら「修正しました」、いま直しているなら「修正しています」、これからなら「修正します」。この三つを文末で書き分ける。

**言い切りの強さを変えない。** 確かめたことは「〜です」、推測は「〜と考えられます」。弱めるのは事実でないときだけ。

**文末を散らすこと自体を目的にしない。** 同じ文末が続いて単調なら、語順と文のまとめ方で整える。文の働き（説明・依頼・報告）は変えない。

## 語彙

**比喩を平易な動詞に戻す。** 次の語は上流の書き直し例で言い換えられたもの。同じ語を機械的に置き換えるのではなく、この種の語を書いたら一度立ち止まる。

| 書いてしまいがち | 言い換え |
| --- | --- |
| 静かに壊れます | 気づかないうちに損なわれます |
| 解像度が一段上がります | 理解が一段深まります |
| 地味に効いてきます | 目立たないながらも役立ちます |
| 時間を溶かす | 時間を無駄にする |
| 原因を潰す | 原因を取り除く |
| 共通側に倒す | 共通のものに統一する |
| 黙ってスキップする | 表に出さずにスキップする |
| 手触り感 | 操作感 |

**道具に意志を貸さない。** 「テストが叫ぶ」「設定が怒る」は、何がどうなるかに書き直す。道具の客観的な動作を述べる文（「この関数は例外を返す」）はそのまま残す。

**大げさな名前にしない。** 仕組みを「OS」「契約」「正本」と呼ぶのは、役割に合う語があるときは避ける。意思決定OS → 意思決定の枠組み。

**「単なるXではなくY」を減らす。** 対比が読み手の判断を変えるときだけ残し、それ以外はYを直接述べる。

## 構成

**結論を最初に置く。** 前置き、経緯、免責を先に並べない。

**予告だけの文を書かない。** 「以下の3点が挙げられます」は、中身を書いてからその文が要るか決める。要るなら中身と同じ一文にまとめる。宣言した数は項目数と一致させる — 一致しないなら数を書かない。

**一段落に一つの話題。** 話題が変わったら段落を変える。段落の最初の文で何の話かが分かるようにする。

**接続詞は、何と何をつないでいるか確かめてから置く。** 「しかし」「そのため」「また」は、前の文との関係が実際にその関係であるときだけ。

**余談は末尾に一文だけ。** 本題の途中に差し込まない。

## 箇条書きと折りたたみ

**太字ラベルとコロンの形を避ける。** 「**検証**: 済み」ではなく、ラベルを説明の文に溶かす — 「検証は済んでいます」。

**箇条書きは、並列が明確なときだけ。** 手順、選択肢、対比する項目。文章で書けるものを項目に割らない。

**`<details>` は検証のためのものを畳む。** 根拠の一覧、再現手順、測定値、引用、棄てた選択肢。summaryは中身を名指しする — 「検証: テスト全件pass」「棄てた選択肢」。中身のないsummaryは、畳んだことが情報を隠しただけになる。

**結論、質問、次の一手は畳まない。** 読み手が行動するために開かずに済むこと。折りたたみは入れ子にしない。

**太字は契約が構造を示すために使う。** 本文の強調には使わない。

## 削る基準

**読み手の次の行動が変わらない情報は、削るか折りたたむ。** 判断材料にならない過程は書かない。

**過程の羅列を結果の一文に置き換える。** 「〜を確認しました。〜も確認しました」は「確認した結果、〜でした」になる。

**同じ結論を二箇所に書かない。** 結論、根拠、次の一手のどれか一箇所に置く。

**測っていないことを、測ったように書かない。** 資料、原文、会話にない数値・原因・感情を足さない。確かめていないことは「確かめていない」と書く。

## 表記

**補助動詞と形式名詞はかなにする。** 出来ます → できます、する事が → することが、〜して下さい → 〜してください。

**それ以外の表記の揺れは直さない。** 送り仮名や英字の大小を整える作業は、読みやすさを上げない。

**英数字の前後の空白は、周囲の書式に合わせる。** 文中で全角と半角を混ぜない。

---

出典: yomiyasu v2.5.0（MIT、https://github.com/nanaism/yomiyasu ）。推敲用の手順（原文との照合、書き手への確認事項の報告）は含めず、生成向けに再構成している。

/engineer

Recompute the "Files upstream no longer ships" list from the manifest **inside the release asset** for the announced tag, not from the repository at that tag — the repository copy is one release behind, so the newest release's deletions never reach the notice. `notify_new_release.ts` and its test are the whole correction; the workflow, the permissions, and the docs stay as they are.

**The defect.** `upstreamManifest()` reads `.github/atomaton-release.json` through the contents API at `latest.tag` and its comment says "the file is the same file" (`src/entrypoints/machinery/notify_new_release.ts:319`). It is not: the copy committed at a tag is this repository's own *deployed* `.github/`, which is the previous release's, so `noLongerShipped(shipped, local.manifest.files)` at `src/entrypoints/machinery/notify_new_release.ts:456` answers "what my release shipped that release T-1 did not ship" rather than "…that release T did not ship". Paths the announced release itself dropped are already present in T-1's list, so they are filtered out and never shown — which is exactly the case the section exists for (`docs/runtime/tasks/move-to-a-newer-release.md:37`, the two workflows removed in v0.1.71 that an adopter keeps forever). The failure is silent: the section renders a plausible, shorter list.

<details><summary>The measurement that shows the read is one release behind, and the shape of the correction</summary>

Measured on the live repository:

| URL | `version` in that file |
| --- | --- |
| `releases/latest` (API) | `tag_name: v0.21.74` |
| `raw.githubusercontent.com/…/v0.21.74/.github/atomaton-release.json` | `"v0.21.73"` |
| `…/v0.21.73/.github/atomaton-release.json` | `"v0.21.72"` |
| `…/v0.21.72/.github/atomaton-release.json` | `"v0.21.71"` |

The shipped manifest cannot lag, so the two files are not the same file: `src/build-dist.ts:231` writes it from `package.json` at build time, and `self/atomaton/scripts/publish-release.sh:46-50` refuses to publish unless the tag equals `v$VERSION`. The zip for v0.21.74 therefore contains a manifest naming v0.21.74 and 96+ paths of *that* release, while the tree GitHub serves at the tag carries v0.21.73's list.

The `Not computed:` degradation and the surrounding logic are right; only the source of the file list changes. Note the wrapper if you go through the asset bytes: `gh()` decodes stdout as UTF-8 and trims it, which is ruinous for a zip, and `ghBytes()` exists for exactly that (`src/adapters/github/gh.ts:107-118`). `gh release download <tag> -p atomaton-delivery.zip` into a temp directory followed by `unzip -p` avoids the problem entirely.

Add the test that would have caught this: a fixture where the manifest at the tag and the release's own manifest differ, asserting that a path the **newest** release dropped is listed. Both existing deletion tests build their upstream manifest from the same value as the latest tag, so they pass whichever version the code reads.

</details>

**What I could not establish.** Two things this repository cannot answer from here, both worth re-reading after a real adoption. First, whether an adopter's `GITHUB_TOKEN` (an installation token for *their* repository) may read `yuma-seno/atomaton`'s public release and contents endpoints at all — here the workflow reads its own repository, so the daily run proves nothing about the case it ships for; if it cannot, the scheduled run goes red in every adopter and never here. Second, whether `gh issue list --search` honours `--state open` (`src/entrypoints/machinery/notify_new_release.ts:359`): the fake `gh` in `src/entrypoints/machinery/testing/harness.ts:109` matches argv by substring and has no idea what the search API does with a state filter, so "one open notice is edited, a closed one is left alone" is pinned only against the fake. If `--state` is dropped when `--search` is present, a closed notice would be edited every day instead of a new one being opened.

I also stopped short of a codebase-wide sweep: the new step's untrusted-input surface (upstream release bodies landing in an adopter's issue body) is the audit's, not this gate's. A read-only delegate I tried to hand the "which places enumerate the shipped workflows" question to died before reaching a model (`402 … free_quota_exhausted`), so I checked that by search here instead.

**What happens next.** The engineer applies the fix above and the pull request comes back to review; nothing else in the change needs to move, and the five checks on it were green. Part C and the template repository stay deferred, as the dispatch named.
